title: OTLP proxy with lazy schema negotiation and tenant-priority queues for tracing ingestion
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Build a lightweight OTLP ingress proxy that can accept heterogeneous tracing clients (OTLP/Zipkin/Jaeger HTTP/gRPC) and route/transform spans to appropriate backend sinks (Tempo, Jaeger, internal S3 archive) with: lazy schema negotiation (detects and adapts to span field variants at runtime), per-tenant priority queues with aging to avoid starvation, and adaptive backpressure/circuit-breakers per backend. Goal is to reduce dropped spans during backend incidents, improve observability SLOs, and simplify downstream exporter logic.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OTLP gRPC and HTTP, Zipkin v2, and Jaeger thrift over HTTP and normalizes to an internal span envelope
Proxy correctly detects backend compatibility and negotiates protocol translation (e.g., convert OTLP->Tempo/Jaeger) without losing key attributes
Per-tenant priority queue honors tenant priority and performs aging: low-priority items promoted after configurable time window
Under synthetic overload (90th percentile production QPS * 3) the proxy sheds low-priority traffic first and preserves high-priority tenant SLOs
End-to-end latency added by proxy < 8ms p50 and < 25ms p95 under normal load
Comprehensive unit and integration tests, and canary rollout plan with automated rollback on error/latency/regression criteria
design_decisions: Use a single binary written in Go for low-latency gRPC + HTTP handling and existing OTLP libraries
Maintain an internal normalized span envelope to avoid nested protocol-specific models in downstream logic

Implement lazy schema negotiation: sample first N spans per connection to infer span field variants (traceid length, status tags, resource attributes) and cache a lightweight compatible transformation plan
Queueing: per-tenant sharded priority queues with token-bucket admission; aging via FIFO promotion after 'promote_after' threshold
Backpressure and spillover: circuit-breaker per-backend; on persistent backend failure, spill to compressed S3 archive and emit a synthetic span pointing to the archive manifest
Security: mTLS for backend connections and support for per-tenant API keys on ingress, masking PII fields according to org policy
rollout_plan: Alpha: deploy to dev cluster behind feature flag; route 0.5% of production ingest from internal tenants
Beta: canary in staging with 5% production traffic, run for 72h with expanded telemetry
Canary: 25% traffic for 48h with active perf and correctness checks
GA: gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring guardrails and automated rollback on criteria
Rollback criteria: increase in span loss > 0.5% vs baseline, p95 latency regression > 30%, elevated error rate for any backend > 1% of requests
test_plan: Unit tests for protocol parsers/converters and transformation plan cache
Integration tests against local instances of Tempo and Jaeger using docker-compose
Chaos tests: kill backend endpoints and validate spillover to S3 + synthetic span creation
Performance: 1h load test using k6 against production-like payload distributions and traceid variants
Compatibility: corpus of spans collected from prod clients (anonymized) used as fixtures to validate lazy negotiation logic
progress_updates: 2025-01-14: Initial design doc drafted in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/OTLP+Proxy+Design (internal link)
2025-01-20: Architecture review with infra and runtime teams; flagged concerns about memory usage for queued spans under extreme tail latency
2025-01-25: Prototype implemented for protocol sniffing and normalized envelope; validated conversion for OTLP->Tempo in local env (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/otlp-proxy/pull/102)

2025-01-28: Load test (dev) at 5x typical QPS found p95 spike caused by heap GC due to unbounded queueing; added per-shard buffer cap and backpressure token-bucket (branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/otlp-proxy/tree/mitigate-buffer-gc)
2025-02-01: Design review follow-up: decided to add compressed spill-to-object-store path and a synthetic-span marker for post-incident reconciliation
2025-02-04: Integration tests against a Tempo canary passed for conversion correctness; started adding Prometheus metrics for queue depth, age-promotions, dropped-counts
